speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is one of Singapore's largest anti-money laundering operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They centre around the effectiveness of Singapore's existing measures to detect and counter money laundering activities; and whether additional measures are needed to curb money laundering in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: My Statement will be in five parts: first, an update on this case and the investigations; second, money laundering risks in international financial centres; third, an overview of Singapore's anti-money laundering regime; fourth, the immigration-related issues that have arisen from this case; and fifth, an outline of our plans to ensure that Singapore's anti-money laundering regime remains robust and effective.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: After my Statement, there will be Statements by Second Minister for Finance and National Development Ms Indranee Rajah, and Minister of State and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) Board Member Mr Alvin Tan.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Murali Pillai, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked whether there were red-flag indicators before the arrests were made and whether the arrested persons will be investigated for running organised crime syndicates or for criminal offences in other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will share what I can, without undermining ongoing investigations by Police.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Police had initially received disparate information on suspicious activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2021, our anti-money laundering regime picked up a few signals, including the use of suspected forged documents to substantiate sources of funds in bank accounts in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) were filed by financial institutions and other companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In early 2022, Police launched a comprehensive, coordinated intelligence probe.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The probe uncovered a web of individuals believed to have connections amongst themselves, including by familial ties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Police analysed the information and probed further, quietly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To avoid alerting the suspects, the work was kept to a very small group of officers, and a decision was made to hold off any enforcement or overt investigative actions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Police's aim was to probe extensively and develop as full a picture as possible of the suspects and their associates, their suspected criminal activities and their assets, before making any move against them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As the probe progressed, the web uncovered by the Police grew and grew.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More and more individuals were implicated in the alleged money laundering operation, and more and more of their assets held in Singapore were discovered.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Police painstakingly and discreetly traced their ties and assets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members would appreciate that anti-money laundering probes of this scale and nature are complex.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Connecting the dots between people and things is a lot easier said than done.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also had to be very discreet, and so Police moved cautiously and with only a very small team.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Had the suspects caught wind of our probes, the suspects and their assets might have fled, and the investigations and the entire operation might have been jeopardised.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Earlier this year, the Police assessed that they had enough information, and consulted the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC).

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: AGC assessed that we had sufficient reason to suspect that criminal offences had been committed in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Following the intensive intelligence probes, extensive reviews of information and examination of evidence, Police moved decisively against the suspects on 15 August this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There has been some speculation circulating in news outlets – internationally and domestically – that this operation was carried out at the behest of China.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore does not need another country to tell us what to do to enforce our laws, nor will we do anything unless it is in our own interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In this case, we started investigations because we suspected that offences had been committed in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So far, 10 persons have been arrested and charged for offences, including laundering criminal proceeds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As investigations are ongoing, I will provide an update to the extent possible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The proceeds likely came from criminal activities that took place outside of Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These include illegal online gambling and unlicensed moneylending.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition to money laundering, some of the accused have been charged with forgery as well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Two of the 10 persons have been charged with additional offences of resisting arrest and perverting the course of justice.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many others, not arrested, are assisting with investigations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Yet, others are wanted by Police for investigations but are not in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Since then, Police have conducted further operations and extensive investigations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As we probe further, there may be more arrests and assets seized.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There has been some interest in how we will deal with the seized assets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The seized assets will be dealt with accordingly and under our laws, depending on the findings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The disposal will be conducted by the Courts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are also ongoing probes by various sectoral regulators, including Government agencies overseeing corporate service providers, real estate agents, financial institutions and others.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Police are working closely with the sectoral regulators and will take action against the companies and individuals should criminal offences be disclosed, such as abetment of money laundering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If there is negligence or non-compliance with anti-money laundering requirements, the sectoral regulators will take action.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some of the arrested individuals made donations to charities in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Edward Chia asked whether these are being investigated.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some charities have decided on their own to ringfence these donations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Others have made Police reports and plan to surrender the monies to the Police.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Commissioner of Charities (COC) will issue an advisory to encourage all charities to review their donor records to ascertain whether they have received donations from the arrested individuals and entities linked to them, and file the requisite STRs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will also include advice to charities on how to handle the monies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We were comprehensive in our actions and operation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will not hesitate to take strong enforcement action against people who would use Singapore as a haven to launder proceeds of crime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will deal with them and their ill-gotten gains to the fullest extent of our laws.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore is an attractive place for investments and businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is political and economic stability, strong rule of law and transparency.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: People are assured that their money is safe here.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore was ranked third in the Global Financial Centres Index last year, behind only New York and London.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our ability to attract international funds has facilitated investments, growth and good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The financial sector contributes about 14% of our gross domestic product (GDP) and employs about 200,000 people.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When we open for business – and we must be – criminals will also try to exploit the same economic openness and our strong reputation for the rule of law, to launder their illicit funds and create the appearance of legitimacy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, all major financial hubs, not just Singapore, are vulnerable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The same characteristics that make them attractive as financial hubs also make them attractive targets for money laundering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Reputable jurisdictions like Singapore take our anti-money laundering responsibilities seriously and pursue cases thoroughly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Ms Foo Mee Har have asked how our efforts compare with others.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This was linked to the laundering of billions of dollars in cryptocurrency stolen from a 2016 hack of Bitfinex, a cryptocurrency exchange registered in the British Virgin Islands.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In January this year, Hong Kong Customs arrested nine persons suspected of 7,600 illicit deals involving over HK$6 billion, which is equivalent to about S$1 billion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The individuals were found to have operated multiple bank accounts for illegal transactions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Earlier this year, in a case similar to ours, the Australian Federal Police charged nine members of an international money laundering syndicate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They had enabled multiple transnational organised crime groups to launder funds derived from criminal activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Australian Federal Police restrained more than AU$150 million – equivalent to about $130 million – in property, cash and luxury items.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Everyone knows that we have a zero-tolerance approach for money laundering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But just as low crime does not mean no crime, zero tolerance does not mean zero occurrence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are under no illusion that we can always keep out dirty money.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As one of the leading international financial centres in the world, the daily transactions in Singapore are voluminous.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have to rely on various stakeholders – the financial institutions and other gatekeepers in the system like corporate service providers, property agents, precious stones and precious metals (PSPM) dealers – to conduct the necessary checks and detect possible risks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A lot of it is picked up and acted upon.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is therefore not the first time that we have taken serious enforcement action against money laundering and breaches of our money laundering requirements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members would recall the transnational case related to 1MDB, involving illicit flows through Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Police extensively investigated the individuals who were suspected of committing offences in Singapore, while MAS thoroughly examined the financial institutions through which the funds flowed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Three bankers were convicted for failure to report suspicious transactions and fined between $10,000 and $128,000 each.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One banker was convicted of offences including money laundering and sentenced to more than four years of imprisonment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Following news of irregularities in Wirecard's financial statements and the alleged involvement of Singapore-based individuals and entities in the matter, MAS closely examined these suspicions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These examples leave no doubt that Singapore takes money laundering seriously.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When there is reasonable suspicion to investigate, we do not hesitate to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We do not turn a blind eye to any risks once we are made aware of them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is not the first time that we have taken serious enforcement action against money laundering offences, nor will it be the last.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even with stringent measures in place, we continuously review our practices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Each time we tighten up, the realistic aim is not to expect that no dirty money will ever come in because that would inevitably also affect legitimate investments and businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Instead, the aim is to reduce risk, have a robust alert system and take prompt enforcement action when we discover such activities as we did in this case.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We must also not fool ourselves into thinking that no news is good news.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Instead, we must have the capability to detect wrongdoings and when we do, have the resolve to act decisively and robustly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we have steadily and systematically built up our anti-money laundering regime over the years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We adopt a holistic ecosystem approach across the Government, public-private partnership and international collaboration.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A whole-of-Government (WOG) effort is led by an inter-agency steering committee co-chaired by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), the Second Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Finance and the Managing Director of MAS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is close partnership between the public and private sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: An example is the Anti-money Laundering/Combating the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Industry Partnership (ACIP).

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Co-chaired by MAS and the Police, ACIP brings together financial institutions to share analyses of emerging money laundering and terrorism financing (ML/TF) risks as well as intelligence on specific cases.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: FATF is an international organisation that sets the global standards to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have been playing an active role in helping to enhance cross-border collaboration and strengthen anti-money laundering controls against new risk typologies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore's anti-money laundering strategy has three prongs and that applies across various sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, prevention, underpinned by a robust legal and regulatory framework to deter criminals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The second prong, detection, is anchored by our STR regime and supervision by sectoral regulators.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our third prong, enforcement, is about taking strong action when there is suspicion of money laundering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have a robust legal and regulatory framework.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Gatekeepers in various sectors have to comply with anti-money laundering requirements, including the conduct of due diligence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MAS requires them to conduct rigorous Know Your Customer (KYC) processes when accounts are opened and CDD on transactions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MAS ensures financial institutions' adherence to the anti-money laundering requirements through close supervision and surveillance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides the financial institutions, designated non-financial businesses and professions (DNFBPs) in other industries are also legally required to conduct KYC and CDD for their customers and transactions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: DNFBPs are gatekeepers in sectors that are known internationally to present higher risks of money laundering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They include real estate agents for property transactions, corporate service providers for company incorporation and dealers of PSPM.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are also DNFBPs that provide professional services, such as lawyers and accountants.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government agencies regulating the respective sectors regularly engage with the gatekeepers to ensure that they adhere to the anti-money laundering requirements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Customers to these financial institutions and DNFBPs are also held accountable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Murali asked whether it is a criminal offence if customers refuse to provide, or provide false or misleading information to commercial entities conducting CDD checks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If financial institutions and DNFBPs assess that certain information from their customer is required for the CDD checks and their customer refuses to provide the information, this should itself raise red flags.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Financial institutions and DNFBPs would be legally required to file an STR if there are reasonable grounds to suspect that a transaction is connected to criminal conduct.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If a customer intentionally provides false or misleading information to commercial entities in order to circumvent the CDD checks, this may constitute a criminal offence under the Penal Code.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Several Members – Mr Zhulkarnain, Ms Hany Soh, Miss Rachel Ong, Mr Don Wee, Mr Murali and Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant – enquired about the anti-money laundering laws related to high-value items.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Precious Stones and Precious Metals (Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing) Act (PSPM Act) covers PSPM and "precious products", which refer to any jewellery, watch or other finished product where at least 50% of its value is attributable to precious stones or precious metals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Simply put, among the items seized, gold bars would be covered by our laws.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some watches and jewelleries would also be covered, depending on the proportion of their value which is attributable to PSPM.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: PSPM dealers are required to perform CDD before they conduct transactions involving cash exceeding $20,000 or where there are reasons to suspect money laundering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As PSPMs may easily be converted to cash, PSPM dealers are also required to file cash transaction reports with the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office (STRO) of the Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) if they conduct transactions involving cash exceeding $20,000.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain asked what measures are in place to ensure that the requirements are not circumvented.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: PSPM are subject to inspections to ensure compliance with our regulations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Appropriate actions are taken against contraventions of the PSPM Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A number of the suspects had purchased high-value assets, such as luxury cars, bags, liquor and ornaments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These were among the assets that were seized or issued with a prohibition of disposal order.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are currently not regulated, unlike, for example, PSPMs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, Singapore's AML/CFT requirements comply with international standards set by FATF, which takes a risk-based approach targeting areas that have been assessed internationally to present higher money laundering risks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will examine if Singapore needs to extend anti-money laundering requirements to new classes of assets beyond what FATF has recommended.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This has to be evaluated carefully so that we do not end up unduly inconveniencing legitimate businesses and customers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The second prong of our AML regime is detection, of which a cornerstone is the STR regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our laws make it a duty for everyone – including but not limited to landlords, property developers, financial institutions and corporate service providers – to report suspicious transactions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Under section 45 of the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act, all persons have a duty to inform STRO if the person knows or has reasonable grounds to suspect, through the course of his profession or business, that any property or transaction they are dealing with may be illicit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is no minimum threshold for STR filing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are also sector-specific requirements to file STRs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Failure to file an STR is an offence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have taken and will take action against those who failed to file an STR when it was merited.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Several Members – Mr Dennis Tan, Ms Sylvia Lim, Mr Vikram Nair, Mr Wee, Ms Ng Ling Ling, Assoc Prof Razwana, Mr Derrick Goh – enquired about our STR regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These queries centre around: (a) the extent to which STRs are filed; (b) whether information obtained from STRs is shared across Government agencies; as well as (c) whether any updates will be made to enhance the effectiveness of our STR regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The reality is that this sheer volume provides easy camouflage for illicit activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Spotting a suspicious transaction among millions is challenging.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To improve effectiveness, STRO has worked with sectoral regulators to develop red flag indicators to improve the detection of money laundering activities by gatekeepers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The red flag indicators are regularly updated to take into account emerging risk types in the money laundering landscape.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That is more than 150 every working day.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over 80% were filed by our financial institutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Intelligence received – whether from STRs, STRO's foreign counterparts, or other sources – is analysed thoroughly and extensively by STRO.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If STRO assesses that the information is relevant, it will disseminate the information to relevant Government agencies which will then conduct further investigations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All this work done by the STRO, sectoral regulators and Police is incredibly difficult.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is not just one needle in a haystack, but one needle in several haystacks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is also not a static field, because determined money launderers are always finding new ways to hide their tracks and avoid detection.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In English): The righteous path is one foot high, the evil path is 10 feet high.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Against this backdrop, it is remarkable that our officers were able to uncover this web and in a fairly short time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: STRO will, of course, continue to update its methods and help agencies better connect the dots.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In February last year, STRO commissioned a new data analytics system to enhance its ability to process large volumes of STRs and raise the quality of financial intelligence disseminated to domestic law enforcement agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But let us understand that this is a never-ending challenge.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With each new case, we will gain fresh insights and enhance our ability to detect the next one.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As Members would know, we take firm enforcement action against money laundering activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how many money laundering- and forgery-related cases involving S$500 million and above have been reported in the past three years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked how we are deepening cooperation with foreign authorities to stem money laundering risks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In February 2021, the Police received information from our international partners and commenced investigations into a case of embezzlement of Angolan state funds that was alleged to have been laundered through foreign banks to Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Another example of our cooperation with international counterparts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We rendered assistance to United Kingdom (UK) law enforcement agencies for the case involving former Formula One boss Bernie Ecclestone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The MAS, SPF and AGC worked closely with the UK authorities on their investigation and prosecution of Ecclestone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore had proactively shared relevant information with our UK counterparts, which helped them develop their case.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Domestic sectoral regulators have also taken to task entities which fell short of their legal obligations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, MAS has taken firm enforcement actions where financial institutions' controls had been unsatisfactory.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members – Ms Foo Mee Har, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, Mr Patrick Tay, Mr Don Wee, Mr Alex Yam, Mr Leong Mun Wai – have filed questions relating to the entry and stay of foreign nationals in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Specifically, how do we scrutinise applications for work passes and other immigration facilities and how we step up checks on high-risk individuals, including those with criminal records or who are wanted in foreign jurisdictions, or who may have used false identities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To recap, 10 persons have been arrested and charged.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As I updated earlier, Police has been casting its net much wider than these 10.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Investigations are ongoing and many persons have been interviewed, and more will be.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They include Singaporeans, Permanent Residents (PRs) and those on different types of immigration passes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Anyone who is found complicit in the wrongdoing after ongoing investigations will be dealt with in accordance with the law, regardless of their immigration status or whether they are Singapore Citizens (SCs).

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have frameworks in place for the assessment of applications for work passes and other long-term immigration facilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The frameworks incorporate information from multiple sources and agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Applicants are screened against a database of blacklisted individuals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We use data analytics to identify and scrutinise higher-risk applications.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Foreigners convicted of an offence in Singapore may be deported from Singapore and in some cases, banned permanently.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Don Wee asked whether we work with foreign governments to verify the information provided by applicants.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Where the agencies have suspicions, we do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our Singapore overseas missions also help to verify the authenticity of the documents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, given the volume of applications, it is not possible to conduct verification checks for all of them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members will appreciate that no screening process is foolproof.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will review how to tighten our verification checks at various points.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the same time, we should be sensible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Most people are not illegal money launderers or criminals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If we make the rules too tight, then it is the vast majority of innocent applicants who will be unnecessarily penalised.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The crooks will still try to find a way around the rules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, we need rules, we need to apply them, but let us be careful about knee-jerk reactions, which may make our business environment unfriendly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: What we need are rules which are internationally accepted and workable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our task is to minimise the risks and increase our ability to catch these persons, without affecting the majority of proper, legal transactions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Should there be further clarifications on the work pass application regime, my colleague, Minister Tan See Leng will address them later.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore has in place a robust anti-money laundering regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are held in high regard internationally not just as a financial centre, but for our strong, principled and no-nonsense approach to taking down individuals who break our laws.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We achieved substantial results in several aspects, even as a few areas were identified for improvement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have moved since the evaluation to address these areas and to further strengthen our regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have updated our prevention frameworks to keep pace with the evolving risks and typologies of money laundering and strengthened our capabilities to proactively detect and take firm enforcement action.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nevertheless, this case is a reminder that even the most stringent preventive measures can be circumvented by determined criminals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But it also shows that our system is able to detect suspicious individuals and activities, and that when we do, we have the resolve and capabilities to track them down and take them to task.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Just as low crime does not mean no crime, zero tolerance of money laundering does not mean zero occurrence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is not the first time Singapore has detected and acted against such money launderers, nor will it be the last.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ministerial Statement on behalf of the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance, Minister of State Alvin Tan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Singapore is one of the world's leading financial centres and our financial institutions handle millions of transactions every single day.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The vast majority of these are legitimate transactions that support the functioning of our economy and allow international trade and investments to be intermediated through Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The international connectedness, diversity and depth of our financial ecosystem also make us attractive to criminals, who will seek to exploit these very qualities to hide their tracks and launder their ill-gotten gains.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For decades now, MAS has been working together with our financial institutions to identify and disrupt such illicit activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Singapore's hard-earned reputation as a trusted and well-governed international financial and trade hub with a strong rule of law, is at stake.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Furthermore, it is the right thing to do.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Our dual objectives of building a dynamic, thriving financial centre on the one hand and maintaining a clean system on the other hand, are mutually reinforcing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: We cannot and will not trade one against the other.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Minister Josephine Teo outlined the Government's three-pronged strategy to deal with money laundering risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The first prong of our strategy is prevention.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS imposes strict AML/CFT requirements on financial institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These requirements are in line with the standards set by FATF and international best practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Amongst these requirements, financial institutions must perform due diligence checks on their customers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This includes verifying their customers' identities and monitoring customer accounts to detect suspicious customer transactions or activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For higher risk customers, financial institutions must perform additional checks to establish if the customer's wealth and funds are legitimate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Where a financial institution detects suspicious customer behaviour, it must promptly report this to the STRO and then take appropriate mitigation measures, such as placing restrictions on the account or where warranted, terminating the customer relationship.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Beyond imposing requirements and expectations on financial institutions, MAS regularly alerts financial institutions to emerging risks and criminal typologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS also publishes guidance papers and circulars to highlight good practices, to raise risk awareness and industry standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS has also strongly encouraged our financial industry to deploy data analytics to further sharpen their detection capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For example, financial institutions have improved their ability to pick up suspicious behaviour amongst their corporate customers and flag specific transactions, characteristics or even networks of concerns by filing STRs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas asked about the anti-money laundering checks conducted on single family offices (SFOs) before tax incentives are granted and whether such incentives have been granted to any of the entities associated with this case.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: All SFOs applying for MAS' tax incentives are required to show proof that they have opened accounts with financial institutions in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Before onboarding the SFOs as customers, MAS expects financial institutions to conduct robust due diligence checks on them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In addition, before granting these tax incentives, MAS screens the individuals and entities involved in the SFO against databases and other information sources for money laundering, terrorism financing and other adverse news.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These SFOs were subject to the checks I just outlined.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The consultation, which just closed last Saturday, 30 September, proposed specific requirements to ensure that all SFOs, regardless of whether they apply for tax incentives, are subject to strict anti-money laundering controls.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For example, SFOs will have to maintain a business relationship with an MAS-regulated financial institution, which will perform anti-money laundering checks on them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The proposed enhancements consulted on go beyond most other leading jurisdictions and financial centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: They aim to ensure that we have quality SFOs that contribute to Singapore and that we keenly watch any money laundering or terrorist financing risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Arising from the findings from this case, MAS will also study whether further measures beyond those that have been proposed in the consultation are necessary, to ensure our approach to SFOs remains robust.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The second prong of our strategy is detection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This involves partnering financial institutions and other agencies to detect bad actors and also tighten our collective defences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The efforts of individual financial institutions or even individual Government agencies are not enough on their own.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Criminals layer their nefarious activities across multiple financial institutions and other parties to evade detection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: To strengthen our detection capabilities, we are introducing the Collaborative Sharing of ML/TF information and Cases (COSMIC).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: I spoke about COSMIC in this House in May this year but will reiterate to refresh Members' memories.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: COSMIC is a digital platform which MAS is co-developing with six major banks in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: It will allow participant financial institutions to share with one another information on customers whose profile or behaviour exhibits potential financial crime concerns, which they currently cannot, due to customer confidentiality obligations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The Bill we passed will allow participating financial institutions to share such information through COSMIC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: One of the key risks COSMIC will target is the misuse of corporate or other legal vehicles to obscure the nature of transactions or the ownership of assets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This is a typology used by the suspects in this case.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: With COSMIC, financial institutions and authorities should be able to detect such risks more promptly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS will permit participant financial institutions to share information they receive from COSMIC with their local as well as overseas affiliates, provided certain conditions to ensure confidentiality are met.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This will prevent bad actors from establishing relationships with overseas affiliates of the six banks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Because of the sensitivity of the information that can be shared on COSMIC, MAS is proceeding carefully with its roll-out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Nevertheless, MAS will review information from COSMIC as part of our overall surveillance efforts and distil key information for sharing with relevant Government agencies and international supervisory counterparts, to combat risks that cut across sectors and borders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Besides upcoming platforms like COSMIC and ongoing partnerships between the public and private sectors and amongst financial institutions, there is also robust collaboration across Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For instance, MAS and MHA co-chair the Risk and Typologies Inter-Agency Group (RTIG).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: RTIG is an interagency body overseeing the identification, assessment and mitigation of ML/TF risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: It involves all relevant supervisory and law enforcement agencies and the STRO.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: RTIG allows agencies to share information on surveillance outputs, such as networks and subjects of concern, for collective action.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These efforts to raise awareness, sharpen detection and tighten collaboration across the industry and Government have borne fruit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: As Minister Teo mentioned, over 80% of STRs filed between 2020 and 2022 were by financial institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The quality of these STRs has improved over time, as STRO and MAS gave guidance and feedback to the financial institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This has facilitated more timely responses to illicit activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This case is a prime example of how this effort has made a difference.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Financial institutions detected many of these illicit activities, filing numerous STRs on the persons of interest prior to the case breaking publicly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These STRs helped law enforcement agencies to identify and take enforcement action against these individuals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In many instances, the financial institutions took additional precautions and actions, including closing these individuals' accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Through RTIG, law enforcement and supervisory agencies were also alerted to similar criminal typologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In April 2022, MAS issued a circular to warn financial institutions of these emerging typologies and engaged major financial institutions to tighten their controls.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: We saw how this close and effective cooperation made an impact on the case as the Police commenced its operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For example, MAS worked closely with our financial institutions to rapidly identify tainted funds so that the Police could seize these funds swiftly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This prevented the suspects from dissipating their ill-gotten gains.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Some of the funds in this case were seized very shortly before there were attempts to move them, because of this close cooperation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Our financial institutions also responded promptly to Police orders to produce information, which helped Police build their case against these subjects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked how surveillance and international partnerships between MAS and other regulators have helped to disrupt money laundering activities and syndicates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: As money laundering networks frequently operate across borders, international cooperation is critical to combating them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS actively works with our international supervisory counterparts on common areas of concern, such as the 1MDB and Wirecard cases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The third thrust of our approach, or the third prong of our approach, is enforcement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This complements the first two prongs of prevention and detection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Where there are breaches of MAS' requirements, MAS takes firm enforcement action against financial institutions as well as key financial institution staff.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: We will not hesitate to take firm enforcement action against errant financial institutions and their key staff, should we encounter similar material weaknesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: I have explained, with examples, how the three key prongs – prevention, detection and enforcement – in MAS' strategy that underpin our financial sectors' defences against ML/TF risks have made an impact, including how they have led to the detection of many of these bad actors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: But we cannot be satisfied with these efforts alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS will also take a critical look at how the suspects were able to access financial services in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Some of them have been charged for presenting forged documents to financial institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This will complement and feed into the work of the Inter-Ministry Taskforce to be led by Minister Indranee, which MAS will also be a part of.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Indeed, there had been some speculation that this money laundering operation has hurt our standing as an international financial centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: On the contrary, I would say that this case is clear evidence of our unflinching commitment to keep Singapore clean.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: While criminals will vary their tactics to conceal their illicit activities, we will deploy all the resources and powers at our disposal to thwart them, bring them to justice and continually strengthen our defences against them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: My colleagues, Minister Josephine Teo and Minister of State Alvin Tan, have spoken about the case, our overall AML regime and the measures we have in place, including in the financial sector.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I will elaborate on two further areas: the real estate sector and companies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The regimes in these areas closely align with our WOG three-pronged strategy outlined by Minister Teo earlier.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: My Statement will be in three parts: first, our restrictions on the foreign ownership of landed residential properties and our controls against money laundering in the real estate sector; second, our regulatory and enforcement measures to deter the misuse of companies; and third, how we will further strengthen our system, incorporating the lessons that we have learnt.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Eight of these properties were landed residential properties at Sentosa Cove.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In addition, 53 commercial properties and five industrial properties have been issued with prohibition orders.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With this in mind, let me explain the framework governing purchases of residential property in Singapore by foreigners.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First and foremost, foreign ownership of landed residential properties is restricted under the Residential Property Act (RPA).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Landed residential properties in Singapore remain primarily the preserve of SCs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Foreigners are not allowed to buy or own landed residential properties without approval.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If approval is given, approved foreign purchasers are only allowed to own one landed residential property in Singapore for their own occupation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms He Ting Ru asked about the grant of approvals.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There are two categories of landed residential property in respect of which approvals can be granted: landed residential properties on mainland Singapore and landed residential property developed with a view to allowing foreign ownership.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The latter is a very small category, that is, the landed residential properties developed in Sentosa Cove.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government takes a very strict approach when granting approvals for foreigners to own landed residential properties in Singapore mainland.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under this regime, applicants must be a Singapore PR for at least five years and must have made exceptional economic contribution to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is assessed considering factors like income tax contributions to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also consider whether applicants have a strong Singapore nexus.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, PRs with children who have served National Service and who have demonstrated strong commitment to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These factors point towards an applicant's connection to Singapore and their long-term commitment and contribution to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The number of approvals granted to foreigners to acquire landed residential properties in Singapore mainland under the RPA remains low.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This should be seen in contrast with our total landed housing stock of more than 73,000 properties and average annual transaction volume of more than 2,700 landed properties on Singapore mainland over the same period.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For the second category of landed residential property, which are those in Sentosa Cove, some of the restrictions are lifted to allow foreigners to buy them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Sentosa Cove was developed as a unique world-class integrated waterfront development aimed at an international clientele.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, foreigners who are non-PRs may acquire landed residential properties in Sentosa Cove and approvals are generally granted.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant asked about the applications and approval numbers for Sentosa Cove.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the past three years, the Singapore Land Authority (SLA) had received a total of 88 applications from foreigners to purchase landed properties in Sentosa Cove.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Since we have set aside landed residential properties primarily for Singaporeans, we do not restrict foreign ownership for non-landed residential properties in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That said, we impose a higher Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty on any residential property purchase by a foreigner.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, the proportion of foreign property purchases is low, at about 2%.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To reiterate, the eight landed residential properties issued with the prohibition of disposal orders are all at Sentosa Cove, where some RPA restrictions are lifted.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: None are landed residential properties on the mainland, where the approval criteria are much stricter.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The rest are non-landed units, which can be purchased by foreigners.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, the requirements of the RPA had been met.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To answer the question filed by Mr Saktiandi Supaat on the impact on the market, while it is difficult to pinpoint the exact effect of the transactions involved in the case on the property market, their impact on property prices is likely to have been minimal.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They make up an insignificant share of residential, commercial and industrial transactions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next, Members have asked about anti-money laundering safeguards in the real estate sector.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Gerald Giam and Ms Hany Soh asked about CDD checks that property agents need to perform and the measures in place to train them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These are valid questions as money laundering is often carried out through asset acquisition and real estate is a valuable and attractive asset class.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We know that there are higher risks of money laundering in the real estate sector and so, we have been working over the years to address this.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have put in place a risk management framework guided by the recommendations made by the FATF.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our framework leverages key sectoral players as DNFBPs with the obligation to look out for red flags and report suspicious transactions to the Police.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This complements other DNFBP professionals involved in real estate transactions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The obligations apply to landed and non-landed residential properties as well as commercial and industrial properties.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the real estate sector, our gatekeepers are: (a) property agents, (b) property agencies; and (c) developers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They are the first line of defence as they are the ones who generally come into contact with parties undertaking real estate transactions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They therefore play an important role in the "prevention" and "detection" of money laundering activities in property transactions – the first two prongs of our anti-money laundering strategy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have progressively strengthened our regime, including enacting various legislation on the anti-money laundering requirements of our gatekeepers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As gatekeepers, each property agent, agency and developer has a duty to perform CDD on their clients or customers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes verifying the identity of the client or the beneficial owner, screening these parties and assessing their level of risk, for example, identifying foreign politically exposed persons, persons from countries or jurisdictions identified by FATF as higher risk, and maintaining records of the relevant documents.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If the customer purports to act on behalf of another party, the gatekeepers must request for the relevant documents authorising such representation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For entities who intend to purchase, the gatekeepers must also check on the nature of its business, ownership and control structure, and place of incorporation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For purchasers from countries where there is a higher risk of money laundering, they are further required to verify their income and the source of their wealth and funds.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The degree of checks required is commensurate with the assessed level of risk, for example, enhanced CDD is required for higher-risk transactions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes verifying the income level, source of wealth or funds of the purchaser.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Given the nature of property development, developers are also required to periodically review the information about purchasers that had been furnished to ensure that it remains accurate and updated until the completion of the property.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Internally, property agencies and developers are also required to implement policies, procedures and controls, such as internal audits to prevent money laundering activities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Failure to do so may result in regulatory action.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Relatedly, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked about guidelines on cash payments.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In general, quantitative thresholds may not be useful as there are many indicators that could point to money laundering activities and any line drawn would be arbitrary.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
